request: Hi , Please create an outlet port on the top right and an inlet port on the bottom left .

parameters.placement: Upper-right corner of the radiator when viewed from the fan-side/right elevation; place through the positive-z end closure in the upper tank region.
parameters.port_axis: Normal to the positive-z end face and directed outward from the radiator.
parameters.port_type: Coolant hose-barb port with an open internal flow passage.
parameters.port_size: Match the existing S05 upper coolant fitting unless a different hose specification is supplied.
parameters.source_geometry: Use the existing upper coolant fitting, face code 0039 / FACE 794, as the dimensional and profile reference.
parameters.clearance: Maintain clearance from the upper-right corner transitions, Fan B shroud, top service cap, and positive-z mounting foot.
parameters.modeling_strategy: Rebuild the invalid single-face fitting as valid parametric solid geometry at the new location, remove the redundant original upper fitting from the bottom-left location, and close its former tank penetration.

actions.target: Top-right region of the existing model. Multiview localization resolves this as the upper portion of the positive-z end of the perimeter frame and upper coolant tank, principally the positive-z end face 0007 / FACE 24. The upper long rail face 0006 / FACE 46 and front upper side panel 0010 / FACE 60 establish the vertical placement. S05 upper coolant fitting 0039 / FACE 794 supplies the matching hose-interface geometry.
actions.relational_constraint: The port must be located on the top-right region. Its bore must penetrate S02 and communicate with the S01 internal coolant passage region, while remaining outside the fin field and clear of S04 Fan B, S06 positive-z mounting foot, S07 top service cap, and the chamfered upper corner. Locate the port in the upper tank volume rather than in the heat-transfer fin field.
actions.unresolved_reference: The multiview images resolve top and right using the fan-side/right elevation, with the positive-z end treated as the right side. Exact hose outside diameter, bore diameter, barb count, wall thickness, and sealing standard are not specified; these should be matched to the existing S05 fittings. Confirm internal tank-wall thickness and coolant-cavity location after repairing or validating the invalid imported STEP topology.
steps: Import the STEP assembly and preserve the original component transforms. Run shape validation and identify the S02 perimeter tank, S01 coolant passage region, S05 fittings, S04 Fan B, S06 mounting feet, and S07 service cap.

Establish the placement convention from the fan-side/right elevation: upper tank is the top edge and the positive-z end is the right edge. Use positive-z end face 0007 / FACE 24 as the primary port-support face.

Inspect upper coolant fitting 0039 / FACE 794 and measure its hose interface, bore, barb major diameter, barb pitch, insertion length, neck diameter, root fillets, and any sealing shoulder. Because this fitting is an invalid single-face solid, use it as a reference rather than directly reusing its topology.

Create a datum point in the upper portion of face 0007. Constrain it below the upper long rail exterior face 0006 / FACE 46, inside the tank wall boundary, and away from the upper chamfer, service cap, fan shroud, and positive-z mounting foot.
Create a datum plane coincident with, or offset just outside, face 0007 and orient it normal to the intended outlet axis.
Sketch concentric circles for the outlet neck outside diameter and coolant bore. Dimension the circles from the measured S05 fitting and fully constrain their center to the top-right datum point.
Extrude or revolve the annular neck outward from the tank end. Join the neck to S02 with a valid Boolean union and provide adequate root wall thickness.

Create the external barb profile in an axial section sketch. Revolve it 360 degrees around the port axis, or use successive conical and cylindrical features, to reproduce the retention profile of fitting 0039.
Apply root fillets between the tank and neck to reduce stress concentration. Add the same lead-in chamfer, tip radius, and barb-edge rounds used by the existing coolant fitting.

Cut the concentric internal bore through the new outlet neck and positive-z tank wall. Terminate the cut at or through the S01 internal coolant passage so the outlet has a continuous fluid path without cutting into the radiator fin field.

Suppress or remove the original upper fitting geometry 0039 / FACE 794 from the bottom-left fitting cluster. If it already has a tank penetration, patch that opening with tank-compatible solid geometry and merge it into S02 while preserving the lower inlet fitting.

Check minimum clearances to Fan B outer shroud faces 0025 and 0029, the positive-z mounting foot 0041, and the top service cap 0043. Move the datum point within the upper-right tank region if required, without entering the chamfered corner.
Perform Boolean and B-rep healing so the rebuilt outlet and tank form valid watertight solids. Confirm that the outlet bore intersects only the intended coolant cavity.

Run an interference check, section view, wall-thickness analysis, and fluid-connectivity inspection. Verify that the final assembly contains one outlet at the top-right and no redundant upper fitting at the bottom-left.

parameters.placement: Lower-left corner of the radiator when viewed from the fan-side/right elevation; place through the negative-z end closure in the lower tank region.
parameters.port_axis: Normal to the negative-z end face and directed outward from the radiator.
parameters.port_type: Coolant hose-barb port with an open internal flow passage.
parameters.port_size: Match the existing S05 lower coolant fitting unless a different hose specification is supplied.
parameters.source_geometry: Use the existing lower coolant fitting, face code 0040 / FACE 795, as the location and profile reference.
parameters.clearance: Maintain clearance from the rounded lower negative-z corner, lower rail walls, Fan A shroud, and negative-z mounting foot.
parameters.modeling_strategy: Retain the existing bottom-left inlet position, but reconstruct the invalid single-face fitting as a valid annular solid and ensure that its bore opens into the coolant tank.

actions.target: Bottom-left region of the existing model. The multiview images show the existing gold fitting cluster at this location. Localize the inlet on the lower portion of the negative-z end face 0005 / FACE 42, adjacent to lower long rail face 0003 / FACE 22 and lower negative-z corner 0004 / FACE 21. Use lower coolant fitting 0040 / FACE 795 as the preferred inlet center and external-profile reference.
actions.relational_constraint: The port must be located on the bottom-left region. Its bore must penetrate the negative-z lower tank wall and connect to the S01 internal coolant passage. Preserve clearance from the rounded lower corner, S03 Fan A, S06 negative-z mounting foot, and all structural rail edges. The inlet should remain separated from the relocated top-right outlet to promote coolant flow across the radiator.
actions.unresolved_reference: The bottom-left location is visually supported by the existing S05 fitting cluster, and the lower fitting is selected as the inlet. Exact bore diameter, hose size, barb standard, required thread or clamp interface, and tank-wall thickness remain unspecified. Match the existing fitting geometry and validate the internal passage after STEP healing.
steps: Use the fan-side/right elevation to establish the bottom-left placement. Select the lower region of negative-z end face 0005 / FACE 42 as the tank interface.

Inspect lower coolant fitting 0040 / FACE 795 and determine whether it contains a real open bore or is only a closed single-face representation. Record its center, axis, overall length, neck diameter, barb dimensions, and clearance to the lower rail.
Create a datum plane normal to the fitting axis and coincident with the negative-z end face. Project the existing lower fitting center onto this plane to retain the demonstrated bottom-left location.
Suppress or remove the invalid lower fitting face body if it cannot be converted into a valid solid. Preserve its measured dimensions and center coordinates as parametric references.

Sketch two concentric circles representing the inlet neck outside diameter and coolant bore. Fully constrain the center relative to lower long rail face 0003 / FACE 22 and negative-z end face 0005 / FACE 42.

Verify that the outside profile does not intersect the lower negative-z rounded corner 0004 / FACE 21 or weaken the corner blend. Shift the center slightly upward or inward if required while remaining in the bottom-left region.
Extrude or revolve the annular inlet neck outward from the negative-z tank wall and Boolean-union it to S02.
Sketch the longitudinal hose-barb profile using the measured lower fitting as reference. Revolve the profile around the inlet axis to create the external retention features and hose insertion tip.
Add an insertion lead-in chamfer, barb-edge radii, and a generous neck-to-tank root fillet consistent with pressure-containing molded or fabricated fittings.

Create a coaxial bore cut through the full fitting length and through the S02 end wall. Extend the bore until it cleanly intersects the S01 lower coolant passage, avoiding the core fins and exterior frame walls.

If the original fitting location already includes a partial or malformed opening, remove overlapping fragments before performing the final cut so there are no internal caps, duplicate walls, or trapped volumes.
Confirm clearance from Fan A rear outer ring 0011, Fan A outer shroud 0015, negative-z mounting foot 0042, and the lower corner radius. Ensure sufficient space for hose installation and a clamp.
Heal and refine the resulting B-rep, merge coincident faces where appropriate, and verify that the inlet neck, tank, and coolant cavity form a continuous watertight pressure boundary.

Use a section analysis to confirm unobstructed communication between the bottom-left inlet and the radiator coolant passage. Check that the final two-port arrangement consists of this inlet and the new top-right outlet.

Perform final interference, wall-thickness, draft or manufacturability, and pressure-boundary checks. Retain the fans, grilles, service cap, mounting feet, and heat-exchanger fin geometry unchanged except where tank connectivity requires local modification.

intention: Provide an outlet for flow to leave the model.
Provide an inlet for flow to enter the model.
Separate the coolant connections diagonally, with the outlet at the top-right and inlet at the bottom-left, to encourage flow through the full heat-exchanger passage region.
Reuse the existing coolant-fitting design language while replacing invalid single-face fitting geometry with valid, manufacturable, watertight port solids.
